turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?
turns.patient_response:
Hey, yeah, thanks. So, what made me come in is that, well, for the past year or so, I've noticed the smallest thing just completely pulls me off what I’m doing before I can even stop it. Like, my phone will buzz, or somebody will walk past my office... which, honestly, is happening a lot more lately since we moved the company to the new building. I told the architects I wanted an open floor plan, you know, transparent leadership, but now I see every single person walking to the breakroom. It's ridiculous. 

Or, I don't know, I'll be looking at a contract and suddenly get a random thought about my in-laws. My mother-in-law is coming to stay with us next month, actually, and she always complains about the guest room mattress. I keep telling my wife we should just buy a new one, maybe one of those memory foam ones you order online, but she wants to go to a real store to test them out. I don't have time for that, running a business and all. The logistics of just getting to the mattress store on a weekend is a nightmare with the traffic on I-95... 

But yeah, wait, what was I saying? Right, just... I get pulled away by every little thing like that before I can even catch myself.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient explicitly states they are easily pulled away from tasks by extraneous stimuli like a phone buzzing or people walking by, as well as by unrelated thoughts.

turns.doctor_question: Looking back, did you struggle with distractibility or staying focused when you were growing up in elementary or middle school?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, actually, looking back, this was definitely around when I was a kid too. My teachers were always moving my seat. Like, constantly. Mostly because I talked way too much, or I'd just get up and walk around without asking, or I'd blurt things out before they even finished the question. 

I remember my sixth-grade teacher, Mr. Davis, he ended up putting my desk right up against his. He drank that cheap diner coffee all day, you know the kind that smells burnt? Reminds me of the coffee machine we used to have in my first warehouse before the business really took off. I finally upgraded us to a really nice commercial espresso machine for the new office last year. Cost an absolute fortune, but you gotta keep the team happy, right? Plus, the beans we get are from this local roaster downtown. The guy who runs it is actually trying to franchise, and he was picking my brain about scaling up operations, since, you know, that's what I do. I told him he needs to lock down his supply chain first because... 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, middle school. But yeah, they were always moving my desk around because I couldn't just sit there quietly.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates distractibility during the interview by going off on a tangent about coffee and forgetting the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient states they would frequently get up and walk around without asking during class.
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient explicitly mentions that they 'talked way too much' as a child.
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient recalls blurting things out before teachers even finished asking their questions.

turns.doctor_question: Nowadays, do you often find yourself feeling restless or having trouble sitting still?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, all the time. It's like... especially when I'm supposed to just sit there and be still. Like during family dinners, or those church volunteer meetings my wife drags me to. It honestly feels like I've got this motor running inside me and I just have to move or do something with my hands, you know? 

Speaking of the church meetings, they're trying to organize this huge summer festival thing, and they put me on the logistics committee because of my business background. But the guy running it, Dave, he means well, but he has zero concept of how to manage vendors. I was looking at the spreadsheet he made for the food trucks, and it's a disaster. I tried to tell him he needs to stagger the arrival times so they aren't all trying to park at once, because that parking lot is tiny. It's the same issue we had at my company's holiday party last year. We rented out this great spot downtown, but the valet situation was a nightmare. I ended up having to go out there and direct traffic myself for like twenty minutes in the freezing cold. I was wearing this new suit I just bought, too, and... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, sitting still. Yeah, I just can't do it. I have to be doing something.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient gets distracted by unrelated thoughts about a church festival and a past holiday party, losing his train of thought and forgetting the doctor's initial question.
symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient mentions needing to 'move or do something with my hands', which indicates fidgeting.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient confirms having trouble sitting still and feeling restless, especially during situations like family dinners or meetings.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient explicitly describes feeling as though he has a 'motor running inside' him.
